title: Vertra product (product.yaml), format v2
description: One product: a container image and the actions it runs. Its image path is derived from its folder, catalog/<team>/<name>/, so it has no image field.

apiVersion.description: The catalog format: vertra.dev/v2. A file without it is from before v2: ./vertra catalog migrate rewrites it.

team.description: The team (team) folder this product is in.

version.description: Its contract's version, 1 when left out. Raise it for a breaking change (an action, input or output removed or retyped, a new required input, a team no longer shared with): vertra catalog check refuses one otherwise, since other teams' templates rely on the contract.

runtime.description: Documentation only: what the image runs on, such as python3.12.

serviceAccount.description: Optional. The Kubernetes ServiceAccount the product runs as, for a cloud identity bound to it. Without one, it runs as default. Not one ending in -api: those are API products' (the gateway mints their tokens).

tokenAudiences.description: Optional. Audiences its steps get a short-lived ServiceAccount token for, to sign in to another cloud by OIDC federation: sts.amazonaws.com (AWS), api://AzureADTokenExchange (Azure), or a GCP workload identity provider. Each is at /platform/tokens/<audience>, its characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by _. Never the cluster's own (the Kubernetes API's); the console refuses those.

check.description: Optional. The action of this product that says whether it's ready on an install: run with no inputs, as the product's identity with its secrets, it outputs ready (true or false), the principal it acts as, and what's missing ([text]). Each install runs it when the product is registered or changes, and daily, and shows the answer with the product. It must change nothing, and can't need an approval, clean up or have a plan.

maxRunning.description: At most this many of the product's steps (all its actions, every run) start or run at once, on each install; the rest wait their turn. For a product whose backend or quota can't take more. Left out: no cap of its own (the install's caps still apply).

clouds.description: Optional. The clouds of the installs it's for (gcp, aws, azure, kind, existing), in place of its team.yaml's. On an install on another cloud it's listed, marked, not checked and not run. Left out: its team's, else every install.

capacity.description: Optional. The capacity its steps run on, where the install offers a choice: spot (cheaper, may be reclaimed: a reclaimed step fails as retryable, so make its actions idempotent) or onDemand (not reclaimed, for steps that mustn't be cut short). Left out: the install's own (usually Spot).

errors.description: What the error codes your actions report mean, and what to do about each: shown on the run page when a step fails with one, beside whether retrying is safe (idempotent) and where to ask your team (team.yaml's help).

means.description: What happened, for the person whose run failed.

do.description: What they can do about it.

deprecated.description: Marks it deprecated, saying what to use instead. It keeps working; the console shows the message to everyone who uses it.

jsonSchemaObject.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for an object.

properties.description: Its fields: each becomes one in the console's form.

script.description: Documentation only: where the action's code is.

secretRefs.description: The team secrets this action uses, each mounted at /platform/secrets/<name>/: its bindings, reviewed with the code that reads them. A team registers the secrets themselves (the console's Secrets tab); keys and description say what each must hold.

shareWith.description: The other teams that may run this action or include it in their templates, or ["*"] for every team. Left out, only its own team.

visibility.description: listed (the default): every team sees this action in the console, and those it isn't shared with can ask for access. hidden: only its own team sees it, so it can't have shareWith.

deprecated.description: Marks it deprecated, saying what to use instead. It keeps working; the console shows the message to everyone who uses it.

idempotent.description: Running it again with the same inputs does no harm: it finds what an earlier attempt made instead of making it twice. Required for maxAttempts above 1, so a step that failed on the platform's side (a reclaimed node, a lost Job, a timeout) is retried only when that's safe.

maxAttempts.description: How many times a step of this action may run in all before it fails: 1 (the default) means no retries. More than 1 needs idempotent: true. A template or DAG may ask for fewer, never more.

concurrencyKey.description: The inputs that name what a step of this action changes (a project, a database). While one step with the same values is starting or running, another waits its turn instead of changing the same thing at once. Values an earlier step produced count too.

approval.description: When a step of this action waits for a person to approve it before it runs: always; otherTeams (only when another team runs it); or a list of teams (only when one of them runs it, so one consumer team needs an approval and another doesn't). A maintainer of this team approves or declines it on the run's page, never the person who ran it; nobody deciding within the install's approval timeout (3 days by default) fails it with APPROVAL_EXPIRED. Left out: never, unless a rule of your team.yaml's allowedTargets asks for one.

cleanup.description: What removes what this action makes or changes, for the resources its steps report in their output's resources ([{type, id, name, link}]). The console records those with the step's inputs and outputs, so they can be deleted months later, after the run itself is gone: deleting one runs action, of this product, as a run of its own. Left out, the console can show what a step made but not delete it.

action.description: The action of this product that removes a resource, such as delete. It must say what it does when the resource is already gone: succeed.

inputs.description: That action's inputs. Left out: {"resource": {...}}, the one resource as reported. Given, exactly these: each a value, or {$input: <name>} (this step's input), {$output: <name>} (its output) or {$resource: type|id|name|link} (the resource's field).

plan.description: The action of this product that says what this one would do, without doing it: given the same inputs, it outputs changes ([{action: create|update|delete|none, type, id, name, detail}]) and an optional summary. The run form offers Preview, and approvers see it. It must change nothing, and can't itself need an approval, clean up or have a plan.

formField.description: One field of the form the console builds from this schema. Any JSON Schema keyword; these hints only shape the form.

x-vertra-order.description: Where the field comes in the form: lower first; fields without one follow, in the order written.

x-vertra-group.description: A heading the field is shown under, with the others that name it.

x-vertra-widget.description: textarea: a big box, for long text.

x-vertra-pattern-message.description: What the field's pattern means, said when a value doesn't match it (instead of the pattern itself).

x-vertra-needs.description: On an input: the kind of thing it names (a wiring type a team defines in teams/<team>/types.yaml, such as gcp.project). A target type is checked against allowedTargets for other teams; Compose offers earlier steps' outputs that provide it.

x-vertra-provides.description: On an output: the kind of thing it is (a wiring type, such as gcp.project), so Compose can wire it into a later step's input that needs it.
